newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APEC to protest unfair treatment of Afghan women.
newsitem.headline: APEC to protest unfair treatment of Afghan women.

text.p: Women leaders from the Asia-Pacific region on Friday condemned the way Afghanistan's new Islamic rulers were treating women and said they would challenge it through the United Nations.
"We'll try to put a stop to it," Imelda Nicolas, chairperson of the Network of Senior Women Leaders from APEC Economies, told Reuters.

Reports of women being beaten in the streets of Kabul have been coming out of Afghanistan since the capital was occupied by the Taleban, a militia group that says it will enforce strict Islamic principles.

The Taleban have told Afghan women not to report to work until their jobs are reorganised to prevent contact with men. Women are expected to remain at home and appear in public only if clad in a "burqa", which covers them from head to foot.

Nicolas said that because Afghanistan is not part of APEC there was little her network could do apart from lobbying against Taleban's treatment of women through the United Nations and other international organisations.
More than 60 women government, business and civic leaders from the 18 members of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum ended a three-day conference in Manila on Friday.
